_comment: Unicode block ranges and writing direction for each language's own native script, keyed by language code. `ranges` is used by check_greek_hebrew_transliteration's phonetic-respelling detector: when validating a file whose language is e.g. 'hi', only the Devanagari range is checked for phonetic-respelling content inside a Greek/Hebrew gloss's transliteration slot — there is no reason to also test for Arabic or Katakana while reviewing a Hindi file. `direction` is used by check_script_boundary_spacing to flag native script glued directly (no space) onto a Greek/Hebrew gloss — only meaningful for 'rtl' languages, since that's what produces a bidi/visual-order bug; 'ltr' entries exist here only for the ranges data. Latin-script languages (de, en, es, fil, fr, pt, ...) are intentionally absent: their own language already IS Latin script, so neither bug class (native-script phonetic respelling, or native-script glued to a gloss) can occur for them by construction — omit them rather than mapping them to an empty range.
